evidence.reason: The current implementation already rejects non-object JSON before any `data.get` access. At the target blob, the parse block (lines 187–192) wraps `json.loads` and adds `if not isinstance(data, dict): raise ValueError('cq output must be an object')` inside the same `try`, so `null`, `[]`, `"x"` and other non-objects fall into the existing `except ValueError` branch returning the 'invalid cq output' error instead of raising AttributeError. A later check (lines 206–207) similarly rejects a non-dict `value`/`result`. History contains the fix commits `99827325` ("Handle malformed cq driver output") and `d82d2fcc` ("Reject falsy non-object driver results"), the latter being the change that rejects non-object driver payloads. The alleged defect no longer exists on the pinned tip.
